behavioral_effects: A coding sandbox starts from a repository-owned runtime image carrying git, GNU make, and uv (plus ripgrep, fd, jq, less, procps), so a target repository's documented entry points can run

The deferred ADR-006 governance smoke test now passes: inside a dev-stack sandbox, git clone --depth 1 of Flux29/fullstack then make governance-check-fast completed with '17 checks run, 0 blocking', matching the host baseline
ADR-006 open question 2 is resolved: egress is a per-stack property of the runtime allowlist entry (base none, dev bridge, prod closed until an allowlist proxy exists)
compatibility_impact: None for existing surfaces. The runtime allowlist alias (workspace) and the default runtime are unchanged, so the RemoteSandbox client path is unaffected; the runtime image swap adds tools without removing anything bare python:3.12-slim offered. New compose-only variable SANDBOX_RUNTIME_IMAGE defaults to the previous image name when unset.
follow_up: Design the production egress allowlist proxy and point the prod runtime entry at it; ADR-006 rule 7 names it as the only path to prod egress
No Make target passes --profile coding; add it to the dev flow so sandboxd and the runtime image build without a hand-typed profile flag
Consider pointing the host-process DockerSandbox default SANDBOX_DOCKER_IMAGE at the workspace runtime image for parity
limitations: The shrink pass deduplicated rationale prose (each fact keeps one canonical home across ADR, compose, Dockerfile) and hoisted the image name into SANDBOX_RUNTIME_IMAGE; the new Dockerfile could not extend an existing file because no other image carries the workspace toolchain, and the build-only service is the smallest compose mechanism for keeping a non-running image current

make governance-preflight cannot run inside a Linux sandbox because preflight-ports shells out to PowerShell; the smoke test targets governance-check-fast, which is POSIX-clean. Full validator parity inside a sandbox was not attempted
The running fullstack-app-1 container predates the sandbox-internal network and was attached to it manually for verification; the next compose recreation of app makes that permanent
reason: A coding workspace sandbox runs bare python:3.12-slim with no make, git, or uv, and no egress to install them - confirmed by 'sh: 1: make: not found' inside a real sandbox - so the agent cannot clone a repository or run its Make targets, and the deferred ADR-006 governance smoke test cannot run. A pinned runtime image carrying those tools, registered as sandboxd's default runtime with an explicitly decided per-stack egress posture, makes a real clone-and-make run possible.
risks: Dev-stack sandboxes reach the public internet and the LAN through the daemon bridge; the standing mitigations are the human approval gate on execute and the workspace ruleset, not the network
SANDBOXD_NETWORK_MODE=none never decides anything while every runtime entry pins its own mode; kept as a fail-closed backstop for a future entry that omits one
rollback: git revert restores the compose files, Dockerfile, ADR, and manifests. A revert does not remove the fullstack-sandbox-runtime:local image from the host daemon (docker rmi separately), does not re-read env into a running sandboxd (compose up -d sandboxd does), and does not delete sandbox workspace state under the sandbox_workspaces volume, including the bootstrap-smoke clone.
security_impact: Widens sandbox egress in the dev stack only, proven behaviorally in both directions rather than by configuration read. Base and prod pin the single runtime allowlist entry to network_mode=none: verified by git ls-remote from inside a sandbox opened through the deployed sandboxd failing with 'Could not resolve host: github.com' (exit 128). The dev overlay grants that entry the daemon default bridge: the same call succeeds (exit 0, HEAD sha returned). A bridged sandbox joins no Compose network, so data-internal services stay unreachable (dev publishes them loopback-only); the Docker socket stays mounted only in sandboxd; the build-only sandbox-runtime service runs true with network_mode none and mounts nothing. The runtime image is digest-pinned (base and uv), replacing the library's build-from-latest coding runtime. Security review of the diff: no findings.
summary: Give coding workspace sandboxes a runtime with make, git, and uv, and decide sandbox egress per stack (ADR-006 open question 2)

validators_run.evidence_ref: pre-existing environment gap, MINIO_ROOT_USER/PASSWORD unset in backend/.env; prod config resolves clean with dummy values for exactly those two and pins the sandbox runtime to network_mode=none
